Saying 'Subhūti, if any bodhisattva resolves this: "dharmas are selfless, dharmas are selfless"' was spoken with respect to two kinds of selflessness: the selflessness of the person and the selflessness of dharmas. Saying 'the Tathāgata states of him "bodhisattva, bodhisattva"' was spoken with respect to the two kinds of completely awakening to those very two kinds of selflessness. If [one asks], 'What is made clear by this?' It is that the apprehension of a person as in 'I will accomplish,' and the apprehension of dharmas as in 'the arrays of the field'—those do not exist for bodhisattvas.

[2-112] source:
བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་མཐོང་བ་དང་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་དབང་དུ་བྱས་ནས། རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས། དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་ལ་ཤའི་སྤྱན་མངའ་སྙམ་མམ་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་ནི་གཟིགས་པ་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་ཕུལ་དུ་བྱུང་བ་མངའ་བ་ཉིད་དུ་ཤེས་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་ཁོ་ན་མངའ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། སྤྱན་རྣམ་པ་ལྔ་མངའ་བ་ཉིད་གསལ་བར་སྟོན་ཏོ། །གཞན་དུ་ན་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་ཁོ་ནས་གཟིགས་པ་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་ཚོལ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་ལ་བསྡུས་ན་སྤྱན་རྣམ་པ་བཞི་སྟེ། གཟུགས་འཛིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་དང་། དོན་དམ་པའི་བདེན་པ་འཛིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་དང་། །ཀུན་རྫོབ་ཀྱི་བདེན་པ་འཛིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་དང་། རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་ཤེས་བྱ་ཐམས་ཅད་འཛིན་པར་བྱེད་པའོ། །གཟུགས་འཛིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་ཡང་རྣམ་པ་གཉིས་ཏེ།ལས་ཀྱི་འབྲས་བུ་དང་། བསྒོམས་པའི་འབྲས་བུའོ། །དེས་ན་རྣམ་པ་ལྔར་འགྱུར་རོ། །རྒྱ་ཆེ་བའི་ཡུལ་ཅན་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་གཟུགས་འཛིན་པ་ནི་དང་པོའོ། །དོན་དམ་པ་མཁྱེན་པའི་དབང་གིས་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་མཁྱེན་པ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་མ་ལོག་པར་འཇུག་སྟེ། དེའི་ཕྱིར་དོན་དམ་པའི་བདེན་པ་འཛིན་པ་སྔ་མའོ། །དེ་ལ་ཆོས་དང་གང་ཟག་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་བརྗོད་པ་ནི་ཆོས་དང་གང་ཟག་ཏུ་བཏགས་པའོ། །དེ་དག་མཁྱེན་པ་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ་སྟེ། འདི་ནི་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་གཟིགས་པ་རྣམ་པར་དག་པའོ། །
[2-112] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of unsurpassable seeing and pristine awareness, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think of this? Do you think the Tathāgata has the fleshly eye?' In order to make known that the Tathāgata possesses the preeminent completely pure seeing, he clearly shows that he does not possess only the eye of prajñā, but possesses five kinds of eyes. Otherwise, completely pure seeing would be sought by the eye of prajñā alone. Regarding that, when abbreviated, there are four kinds of eyes: that which apprehends form, that which apprehends the ultimate truth, that which apprehends the relative truth, and that which apprehends all objects of knowledge in all aspects. That which apprehends form is also of two kinds: the result of karma and the result of meditation. Therefore, there become five kinds. Because of possessing an extensive object, that which apprehends form is the first. By the power of knowing the ultimate, the knowledge of the relative engages unmistakably; therefore, that which apprehends the ultimate truth is prior. Regarding that, what is manifestly expressed as dharmas and persons is imputed as dharmas and persons. Knowing those is to be called the eye of dharma; this is the completely pure seeing of however much there is.

translation: With respect to the perfection of mind, the establishment of mindfulness, it was extensively spoken: 'Bhagavān, in the future time, having heard such a teaching of the Dharma as this...' By this, the reason why the Bhagavān established his intention upon whichever sentient beings is completely and clearly taught: that they are not sentient beings is from the ultimate. That they are not without being sentient beings is from the conventional. What is other than this is from the teaching of the ultimate. Clearly teaching the meaning of the reasoning for the uncommon meanings is exactly as before for those very things.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: With respect to the perfection of mind, manifestly perfect awakening, it was extensively spoken: 'Do you think there is any Dharma at all by which the Tathāgata manifestly perfectly awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?' Regarding that, having completely abandoned the fault of the view 'there is no such Dharma whatsoever', one completely seeks awakening and the path of awakening; moreover, that is taught by the two awakenings and the two definitive words. That is by grasping the word 'unsurpassed' and the word 'perfect'. 'a nu ra bi ta tra dharmo na bidya te' is grasping the word anuttara; it teaches the specific characteristic of awakening. In that awakening which has the characteristic of complete liberation, there is not even a particle of an arising dharma; for that very reason, it is unapprehendable. By that very thing, it should be known that 'rjes su yong', 'de la chos', 'yod pa', and 'na' mean 'does not exist'.

translation: What is the intention behind saying, 'By that itself, the Tathāgata would have the grasping at a self'? What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

translation: If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

Being without annihilation is by individual realization; since the dharmas of saṃsāra have been mastered as being like reflections and emanations, one again thoroughly engages in the welfare of sentient beings. By this, for the time being, through refuting the suchness that goes exclusively to peace, the non-abiding in nirvāṇa itself is clearly taught.

With respect to the perfection of mind, the establishment of the great meaning, it was extensively spoken: 'however many Mount Merus there are in the three-thousand great thousand world system'.

[2-127] source:
དོན་ཆེན་པོ་གདམས་ངག་རྣམ་པར་བཞག་པའི་དབང་དུ་བྱས་ནས། དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་འདི་སྙམ་དུ་ངས་སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་བཀྲོལ་ལོ་ཞེས་དགོངས་སོ་སྙམ་ན་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་སོ། །
[2-127] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the establishment of the great meaning, the instructions, it was extensively spoken: 'if one thinks the Tathāgata thinks this: "I have liberated sentient beings"'.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: Then, in order to thoroughly abandon associating with complete affliction in saṃsāra while non-abiding in nirvāṇa, it was thus extensively spoken: 'Moreover, Subhūti, if a son of noble family...'. Regarding that, if it is asked what is the meaning of 'to the dharmas that are selfless and without arising', the mastery found by the Tathāgata over the emanation-like nature of the thorough engagement of whatever dharma, which is not the nature of the dharmas of saṃsāra and likewise which does not arise from karma and afflictions and which has become mastered, is called 'selfless and without arising'. If it is asked what makes this known: since even elsewhere if by completely grasping the merit just as it was explained one does not become completely afflicted in saṃsāra, what need to mention the Bodhisattvas' patience regarding the selfless and without arising? It is because by attaining patience for non-arising, much more merit will arise.

[2-130] source:
བྱིས་པ་སོ་སོའི་སྐྱེ་བོ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་དེ་ཡོད་པར་བཟུང་ཡང་བཟུང་དུ་མེད་དོ་ཞེས་པ་ནི། རབ་འབྱོར་བྱིས་པ་སོ་སོའི་སྐྱེ་བོ་རྣམས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི། དེ་དག་སྐྱེ་བོ་མེད་པར་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་ཏེ་དེ་རྣམས་དེ་བཞིན་ནོ། །

[2-131] source:
ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་པའི་དབང་དུ་བྱས་ནས། རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པས་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་ལ་ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པ་དང་པོས་ནི་ཇི་ལྟར་མི་མཐོང་བ་དང་གང་གིས་མི་མཐོང་བ་གསལ་བར་བསྟན་ཏེ། ཅི་ལྟར་མི་མཐོང་ཞེ་ན་ལྟ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཐ་སྙད་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་སོ། །སྤོང་བར་བརྗོད་པ་ནི་བསམ་གཏན་ཏེ་གང་གི་བསམ་གཏན་པ་དེ་ལྟར་སྤོང་བ་པ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པ་སྟེ། དེ་ཡང་བསམ་པ་དང་སྒོམ་པའོ། །དེ་ལ་བསམ་པས་ནི་དེ་མ་ཡིན་པར་བཟུང་ལ། བསྒོམས་པས་ནི་ལོག་པར་ཤེས་པ་སྟེ། སྤོང་བས་ཞུགས་པས་ནི་ལོག་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཐ་སྙད་བཟུང་བར་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །གང་གིས་མི་མཐོང་ཞེ་ན་ཐ་སྙད་ལ་ཞུགས་པའི་སྐྱེ་བོ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་སོ། །
[2-131] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

[2-132] source:
ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པ་གཉིས་པའི་ཕྱེད་སྔ་མས་ནི་གང་མི་མཐོང་བ་དང་ཕྱེད་ཕྱི་མས་ནི་རྒྱུ་གང་གིས་མི་མཐོང་བ་གསལ་བར་བསྟན་ཏེ། དེ་ལ། སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ནི་ཆོས་ཉིད་བལྟ། །ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཆོས་འདི་ལ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི་དོན་དུ་དགོངས་པའོ། །

By the former half of the second verse, what one does not see, and by the latter half, by what cause one does not see, are clearly taught. Regarding that, 'the Buddhas are to be seen as Dharmatā' is thinking of this Dharma as the meaning of the Tathāgata.

[2-133] source:
རྒྱུ་གང་གི་ཤེས་ན། འདྲེན་པ་རྣམས་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ། །ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་ལ་དམིགས་པ་ཀུན་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པའི་སྐུ་སྟེ། དེའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་རྣམས་ཆོས་ཉིད་དུ་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྟེ་འདི་ནི་དེར་བལྟའོ། །ཅི་སླར་ཡང་རྒྱུ་གང་གིས་བལྟ་བྱ་མ་ཡིན་ཞེ་ན། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཆོས་ཉིད་ནི་སྒྲ་ཇི་བཞིན་པས་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ལ། སོ་སོ་རང་གིས་རིག་པར་བྱ་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་སྒྲ་ཇི་བཞིན་མ་ཡིན་པས་ཀྱང་མི་མཐོང་བས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་མི་ནུས་ཞེས་ཏེ། དོན་འདི་གསལ་བར་སྟོན་པ་ནི། ཆོས་ཉིད་ཤེས་པར་བྱ་མིན་པས། །དེས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་མི་ནུས། །ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་འདིར་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུའི་རྟེན་ནི་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པ་ནི། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པས་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པས་སྟོན་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའོ། །
[2-133] translation already produced for this document:
If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

[2-134] source:
མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་རྒྱུ་ལས་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་བརྙེས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པ་སྤང་བའི་ཕྱིར་དུ་འདི་ལྟར། རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་འཛིན་ན་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེ་རྣམ་ལ་ནི་དེ་ལྟ་བུའོ། །
[2-134] translation already produced for this document:
In order to abandon the manifest attachment thinking that from the cause of the perfection of marks one found unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening, it was thus extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? If you hold the thought that by the perfection of marks one manifestly perfectly awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening'; for those, it is like that.

[2-135] source:
ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་འཁོར་བ་དང་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་དབང་དུ་བྱས་ནས། རབ་འབྱོར་ཡང་ཁྱོད་སྙམ་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐེག་པ་ལ་ཡང་དག་པར་ཞུགས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་ཆོས་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་བཤིག་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་པ་ནི། ཇི་ལྟར་གནས་པའི་ཆོས་ཉིད་དོ། །ཆད་པ་མེད་པ་ནི་སོ་སོར་རྟོགས་པས་ཏེ་འཁོར་བ་པའི་ཆོས་རྣམས་གཟུགས་བརྙན་དང་སྤྲུལ་པ་ལྟ་བུར་དབང་དུ་གྱུར་པས་སླར་ཡང་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་ལ་རབ་ཏུ་འཇུག་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །འདིས་ནི་རེ་ཞིག་ཞི་བ་བགྲོད་པ་གཅིག་པུ་པའི་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་བཀག་པས་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ལ་རབ་ཏུ་མི་གནས་པ་ཉིད་གསལ་བར་བསྟན་ཏོ། །

With respect to the perfection of mind, the non-abiding in saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, moreover if you think "by those who have correctly entered the Bodhisattva vehicle"'. Regarding that, not designating the destruction of any dharma whatsoever is Dharmatā just as it abides. Being without annihilation is by individual realization; since the dharmas of saṃsāra have been mastered as being like reflections and emanations, one again thoroughly engages in the welfare of sentient beings. heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: 'Moreover, Subhūti, a Bodhisattva should not completely grasp a heap of merit' clearly teaches the very non-abiding in saṃsāra; by not thoroughly abiding in saṃsāra, one completely grasps a heap of merit.

[2-131] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

[2-132] source:
ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པ་གཉིས་པའི་ཕྱེད་སྔ་མས་ནི་གང་མི་མཐོང་བ་དང་ཕྱེད་ཕྱི་མས་ནི་རྒྱུ་གང་གིས་མི་མཐོང་བ་གསལ་བར་བསྟན་ཏེ། དེ་ལ། སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ནི་ཆོས་ཉིད་བལྟ། །ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཆོས་འདི་ལ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི་དོན་དུ་དགོངས་པའོ། །

[2-133] source:
རྒྱུ་གང་གི་ཤེས་ན། འདྲེན་པ་རྣམས་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ། །ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་ལ་དམིགས་པ་ཀུན་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པའི་སྐུ་སྟེ། དེའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་རྣམས་ཆོས་ཉིད་དུ་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྟེ་འདི་ནི་དེར་བལྟའོ། །ཅི་སླར་ཡང་རྒྱུ་གང་གིས་བལྟ་བྱ་མ་ཡིན་ཞེ་ན། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཆོས་ཉིད་ནི་སྒྲ་ཇི་བཞིན་པས་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ལ། སོ་སོ་རང་གིས་རིག་པར་བྱ་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་སྒྲ་ཇི་བཞིན་མ་ཡིན་པས་ཀྱང་མི་མཐོང་བས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་མི་ནུས་ཞེས་ཏེ། དོན་འདི་གསལ་བར་སྟོན་པ་ནི། ཆོས་ཉིད་ཤེས་པར་བྱ་མིན་པས། །དེས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་མི་ནུས། །ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་འདིར་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུའི་རྟེན་ནི་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པ་ནི། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པས་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པས་སྟོན་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའོ། །
[2-133] translation already produced for this document:
If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

[2-134] source:
མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་རྒྱུ་ལས་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་བརྙེས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པ་སྤང་བའི་ཕྱིར་དུ་འདི་ལྟར། རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་འཛིན་ན་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེ་རྣམ་ལ་ནི་དེ་ལྟ་བུའོ། །

In order to abandon the manifest attachment thinking that from the cause of the perfection of marks one found unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening, it was thus extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

With respect to the perfection of mind, the non-abiding in saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, moreover if you think "by those who have correctly entered the Bodhisattva vehicle"'. heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: The Bhagavat stated: 'Although one completely grasps, one does not grasp wrongly; thus "one should completely grasp" teaches what is to be completely grasped by an enumeration. How one does not grasp wrongly is just as previously explained; it is exactly those.'

[2-131] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

[2-133] translation already produced for this document:
If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་འཁོར་བ་དང་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་དབང་དུ་བྱས་ནས། རབ་འབྱོར་ཡང་ཁྱོད་སྙམ་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐེག་པ་ལ་ཡང་དག་པར་ཞུགས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་ཆོས་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་བཤིག་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་པ་ནི། ཇི་ལྟར་གནས་པའི་ཆོས་ཉིད་དོ། །ཆད་པ་མེད་པ་ནི་སོ་སོར་རྟོགས་པས་ཏེ་འཁོར་བ་པའི་ཆོས་རྣམས་གཟུགས་བརྙན་དང་སྤྲུལ་པ་ལྟ་བུར་དབང་དུ་གྱུར་པས་སླར་ཡང་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་ལ་རབ་ཏུ་འཇུག་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །འདིས་ནི་རེ་ཞིག་ཞི་བ་བགྲོད་པ་གཅིག་པུ་པའི་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་བཀག་པས་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ལ་རབ་ཏུ་མི་གནས་པ་ཉིད་གསལ་བར་བསྟན་ཏོ། །
[2-135] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the non-abiding in saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, moreover if you think "by those who have correctly entered the Bodhisattva vehicle"'. Regarding that, not designating the destruction of any dharma whatsoever is Dharmatā just as it abides. Being without annihilation is by individual realization; since the dharmas of saṃsāra have been mastered as being like reflections and emanations, one again thoroughly engages in the welfare of sentient beings. By this, for the time being, through refuting the suchness that goes exclusively to peace, the non-abiding in nirvāṇa itself is clearly taught.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: With respect to the perfection of mind, the deportment of moving and abiding, it was extensively spoken: 'Moreover, Subhūti, whoever would speak thus: "the Tathāgata went or came"'. Regarding that, moving is walking and standing. The rest is deportment.

[2-131] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

[2-132] source:
ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པ་གཉིས་པའི་ཕྱེད་སྔ་མས་ནི་གང་མི་མཐོང་བ་དང་ཕྱེད་ཕྱི་མས་ནི་རྒྱུ་གང་གིས་མི་མཐོང་བ་གསལ་བར་བསྟན་ཏེ། དེ་ལ། སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ནི་ཆོས་ཉིད་བལྟ། །ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཆོས་འདི་ལ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི་དོན་དུ་དགོངས་པའོ། །

[2-133] source:
རྒྱུ་གང་གི་ཤེས་ན། འདྲེན་པ་རྣམས་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ། །ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་ལ་དམིགས་པ་ཀུན་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པའི་སྐུ་སྟེ། དེའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་རྣམས་ཆོས་ཉིད་དུ་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྟེ་འདི་ནི་དེར་བལྟའོ། །ཅི་སླར་ཡང་རྒྱུ་གང་གིས་བལྟ་བྱ་མ་ཡིན་ཞེ་ན། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཆོས་ཉིད་ནི་སྒྲ་ཇི་བཞིན་པས་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་ལ། སོ་སོ་རང་གིས་རིག་པར་བྱ་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་སྒྲ་ཇི་བཞིན་མ་ཡིན་པས་ཀྱང་མི་མཐོང་བས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་མི་ནུས་ཞེས་ཏེ། དོན་འདི་གསལ་བར་སྟོན་པ་ནི། ཆོས་ཉིད་ཤེས་པར་བྱ་མིན་པས། །དེས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་མི་ནུས། །ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་འདིར་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུའི་རྟེན་ནི་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པ་ནི། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པས་མ་ཡིན་ཞེས་པས་སྟོན་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བལྟ་བར་བྱ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའོ། །
[2-133] translation already produced for this document:
If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

[2-134] source:
མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་རྒྱུ་ལས་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་བརྙེས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པ་སྤང་བའི་ཕྱིར་དུ་འདི་ལྟར། རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་འཛིན་ན་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེ་རྣམ་ལ་ནི་དེ་ལྟ་བུའོ། །
[2-134] translation already produced for this document:
In order to abandon the manifest attachment thinking that from the cause of the perfection of marks one found unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening, it was thus extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? If you hold the thought that by the perfection of marks one manifestly perfectly awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening'; for those, it is like that.

With respect to the perfection of mind, the non-abiding in saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, moreover if you think "by those who have correctly entered the Bodhisattva vehicle"'. Regarding that, not designating the destruction of any dharma whatsoever is Dharmatā just as it abides. Being without annihilation is by individual realization; since the dharmas of saṃsāra have been mastered as being like reflections and emanations, one again thoroughly engages in the welfare of sentient beings. heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: With respect to moving and abiding, having obtained mastery over the meditation on the body of form and name, it was extensively spoken: 'Moreover, Subhūti, if any son of noble family or daughter of noble family... however many particles of earth there are in the great trichiliocosm world system'. Here also there are the method of making subtle and the method of making non-apparent; their meditation should be known as before. By 'do you think that collection of subtle particles is many?', here it refers to 'however many', which is the method of making subtle.

[2-131] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

[2-133] translation already produced for this document:
If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

[2-134] source:
མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་རྒྱུ་ལས་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་བརྙེས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པ་སྤང་བའི་ཕྱིར་དུ་འདི་ལྟར། རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས། མཚན་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་སོ་སྙམ་དུ་འཛིན་ན་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་གསུངས་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེ་རྣམ་ལ་ནི་དེ་ལྟ་བུའོ། །

[2-131] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

[2-133] translation already produced for this document:
If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

[2-134] source:

With respect to the perfection of mind, the complete apprehension of the Dharmakāya, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?'. Regarding that, by the first verse, how one does not see and by whom one does not see are clearly taught. If it is asked how one does not see, it is by the conventions of seeing and so forth. What is expressed as abandoning is meditation; it is expressed that one whose meditation is that is thus an abandoner, and that is also thinking and meditating. Regarding that, by thinking, one grasps it as not being that, and by meditating, it is wrong knowing; thus by having engaged through abandoning, one should know that the convention of wrong knowing is grasped. If it is asked by whom one does not see, it is by the beings who have engaged in conventions.

If it is asked by what cause it is known, it was spoken: 'the guides are the Dharmakāya'. Because the Buddhas whose observing of suchness goes everywhere are the completely pure body, therefore they are to be seen as Dharmatā; this is to be seen as that. If it is asked moreover by what cause is it not to be seen, because Dharmatā, the characteristic of suchness, is not to be cognized literally, and because it is exactly to be individually reflexively known, by not being literal, through not seeing, one is not able to cognize; clearly teaching this meaning, it was spoken: 'since Dharmatā is not to be known, / by that one is not able to cognize'. Likewise here, that the support of the Dharmakāya is not to be seen as the Tathāgata is taught by 'not by the perfection of marks': the perfection of marks is not to be seen as the Tathāgata.

[2-135] translation already produced for this document:
With respect to the perfection of mind, the non-abiding in saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, it was extensively spoken: 'Subhūti, moreover if you think "by those who have correctly entered the Bodhisattva vehicle"'. Regarding that, not designating the destruction of any dharma whatsoever is Dharmatā just as it abides. Being without annihilation is by individual realization; since the dharmas of saṃsāra have been mastered as being like reflections and emanations, one again thoroughly engages in the welfare of sentient beings. By this, for the time being, through refuting the suchness that goes exclusively to peace, the non-abiding in nirvāṇa itself is clearly taught.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: If it is asked why it is restated that whatever is a collection of subtle particles is unestablished in the nature of a collection, which becomes the idea of a collection even when the other is not explained: knowing that the Tathāgata has spoken of it as a non-realm is the very method of making non-apparent, and meditation on the body of name should be known as before. Here, the world of the three realms intends the world of sentient beings, and that is also completely distinguished by the collection of names.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: 'Bhagavat, if a world system existed, it would be grasped as a whole' was spoken with respect to both whatever is a world system and whatever are subtle particles. Grasping as a whole is of two aspects: grasping as a whole as a single unit, and grasping as a whole by distinguishing. Regarding those, what exists in a world system would be grasped as a whole as a single unit as 'sentient beings in the aggregates'; what exists in subtle particles would be grasped as a whole by distinguishing, as it is grasped as a whole by grasping a collection of subtle particles.

translation: If it is asked how: what is expressed as self by other non-Buddhists and what is spoken of as self by the Tathāgata are posited as the selflessness of persons. Speaking of that view of self as a non-view posits the selflessness of phenomena; if one applies it such that there is no grasping at a view regarding that view of self, one will attain meditative absorption in yoga; thus that non-conceptualization is the method for entering it.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: 'Subhūti, thus one who has rightly entered the vehicle of the bodhisattvas', this completely teaches who does not conceptualize. 'All phenomena', this teaches regarding what one should not conceptualize. 'Should be known, should be viewed, should be resolved upon', this teaches that by which one should not conceptualize, namely, by knowing, seeing, and resolving, beginning from the higher mind and higher wisdom. Regarding those, what relies on serenity is wisdom. What relies on insight is exalted knowledge. Both seeings are here the samādhi of resolution; by the power of samādhi one intensely resolves upon the objective support of a reflected image.

translation: By 'one should resolve in such a way that one does not abide even in the perception of a phenomenon', whatever is conceptualization is completely taught; it is exactly those. Although that is so, it is to be completely illuminated in such a way that one does not become afflicted at all.

'Subhūti, thus one who has rightly entered the vehicle of the bodhisattvas', this completely teaches who does not conceptualize. 'All phenomena', this teaches regarding what one should not conceptualize. 'Should be known, should be viewed, should be resolved upon', this teaches that by which one should not conceptualize, namely, by knowing, seeing, and resolving, beginning from the higher mind and higher wisdom. Regarding those, what relies on serenity is wisdom. What relies on insight is exalted knowledge. Both seeings are here the samādhi of resolution; by the power of samādhi one intensely resolves upon the objective support of a reflected image.

ཅི་ནས་ཆོས་སུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་ལ་ཡང་མི་གནས་པ་དེ་ལྟར་མོས་པར་བྱའོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བས་ནི། རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ཡོངས་སུ་བསྟན་ཏེ་དེ་རྣམས་ནི་ཉིད་དོ། །ཆོས་སུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པས་ནི་ཐུན་མོང་མ་ཡིན་པའི་དོན་གྱི་རིགས་པའི་དོན་སྟོན་པར་བྱེད་དེ། འདི་ནི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་ལ་སྙོམས་པར་འཇུག་པའི་ཐབས་ཏེ་རྟེན་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །འདུན་པ་དང་སྨོན་ལམ་དང་རྣམ་པར་གཡེང་བ་ཚར་གཅོད་པ་སྟེ་དེ་ཙམ་ཉིད་དུ་བྱའོ། །དེའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་དག་གིས་ཐབས་བཤད་ཟིན་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟ་བུ་ཉིད་དོ། །
[2-151] translation already produced for this document:
By 'one should resolve in such a way that one does not abide even in the perception of a phenomenon', whatever is conceptualization is completely taught; it is exactly those. 'The perception of a phenomenon' teaches the logical meaning of the uncommon meaning; this is the method of meditative absorption into yoga and should be known in all bases. Aspiration, prayer, and eradicating distraction are to be done to exactly that extent. Therefore, the method has been explained by those; it is exactly like that.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
translation: If it is asked how one correctly completely teaches: It is in such a way that one does not completely teach at all; therefore it is called 'correctly completely teaching'. If it is asked what the intention of this is: The Dharma whose nature is taught as inexpressible is not something to be taught; otherwise, it would be taught with affliction, because the meaning would be mistaken; teaching it in that way, there is no intense faith and seeking. Therefore, the Dharma is taught without affliction; that is exactly like that.

རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ལྟར་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐེག་པ་ལ་ཡང་དག་པར་ཞགས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་འདི་ནི་སུ་རྣམ་པར་མི་རྟོག་པར་བྱེད་པ་དེ་ཡོངས་སུ་བསྟན་ཏོ། །ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་ཅེས་བྱ་བ་འདིས་ནི་གང་ལ་རྣམ་པར་མི་རྟོག་པར་བྱ་བ་དེ་བསྟན་ཏོ། །ཤེས་པར་བྱ་བ་ལྟ་བར་བྱ་མོས་པར་བྱ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་འདིས་ནི་ལྷག་པའི་སེམས་དང་ལྷག་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ལས་བརྩམས་ཏེ། ཤེས་པ་དང་མཐོང་བ་དང་མོས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཏེ། གང་གིས་རྣམ་པར་མི་རྟོག་པར་བྱ་བ་དེ་བསྟན་ཏོ། །དེ་ལ་ཞི་གནས་ལ་བརྟེན་པ་ནི་ཤེས་རབ་བོ། །ལྷག་མཐོང་ལ་བརྟེན་པ་ནི་ཡེ་ཤེས་སོ། །མཐོང་བ་གཉི་ག་ཡང་འདིར་མོས་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ཏེ། ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་དབང་གིས་གཟུགས་བརྙན་གྱི་དམིགས་པ་ལ་ལྷག་པར་མོས་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །
[2-150] translation already produced for this document:
'Subhūti, thus one who has rightly entered the vehicle of the bodhisattvas', this completely teaches who does not conceptualize. 'All phenomena', this teaches regarding what one should not conceptualize. 'Should be known, should be viewed, should be resolved upon', this teaches that by which one should not conceptualize, namely, by knowing, seeing, and resolving, beginning from the higher mind and higher wisdom. Regarding those, what relies on serenity is wisdom. What relies on insight is exalted knowledge. Both seeings are here the samādhi of resolution; by the power of samādhi one intensely resolves upon the objective support of a reflected image.

[2-151] source:
ཅི་ནས་ཆོས་སུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་ལ་ཡང་མི་གནས་པ་དེ་ལྟར་མོས་པར་བྱའོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བས་ནི། རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ཡོངས་སུ་བསྟན་ཏེ་དེ་རྣམས་ནི་ཉིད་དོ། །ཆོས་སུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པས་ནི་ཐུན་མོང་མ་ཡིན་པའི་དོན་གྱི་རིགས་པའི་དོན་སྟོན་པར་བྱེད་དེ། འདི་ནི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་ལ་སྙོམས་པར་འཇུག་པའི་ཐབས་ཏེ་རྟེན་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་རིག་པར་བྱའོ། །འདུན་པ་དང་སྨོན་ལམ་དང་རྣམ་པར་གཡེང་བ་ཚར་གཅོད་པ་སྟེ་དེ་ཙམ་ཉིད་དུ་བྱའོ། །དེའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་དག་གིས་ཐབས་བཤད་ཟིན་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟ་བུ་ཉིད་དོ། །
[2-151] translation already produced for this document:
By 'one should resolve in such a way that one does not abide even in the perception of a phenomenon', whatever is conceptualization is completely taught; it is exactly those. 'The perception of a phenomenon' teaches the logical meaning of the uncommon meaning; this is the method of meditative absorption into yoga and should be known in all bases. Aspiration, prayer, and eradicating distraction are to be done to exactly that extent. Therefore, the method has been explained by those; it is exactly like that.

heading: ཐུགས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ།
source: ཨེ་ཏཱ་ད་ཤཱི་མརྠ་ག་ཏིཾ་ནི་ཤཱ་མྱ། ཡེ་ཥཱཾ་མ་ཧཱ་ཡཱ་ན་མ་བདྡྷཽ་མེ་བ། ཏཱ་ནསྨནོ་བེདྨི་ན་བཱསྨ་ནོ་པི། གུ་ཎཻ་ར་བྷཱ་བྱཱ་ནླ་སུ་ནཱ་ན་བཻ་མི། ཧཱི་ནོ་ཧི་གཱམྦྷཱིཪྻ་མུ་དཱ་ར་ཏཱམྦཱ། བོདྡྷུནྣ་ཤཀྣཱ་ཏི་ན་ཙཱ་དྷི། མོཀྟུཾ། པྲཱ་ཡེ་ཎ་ཙོཾ་བཾ་བི་དྷ་ཨེ་ཥ་ལོ་ཀཿ ཏེ་ནཱ་ཏྲ་དྷརྨེ་ཁི་ལ་ཏཱམྤྲ་ཡཱ་ཏཿ འཕགས་པ་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པའི་གནས་བདུན་གྱི་རྒྱ་ཆེར་འགྲེལ་པ། སློབ་དཔོན་དབྱིག་གཉེན་གྱིས་མཛད་པ་རྫོགས་སོ།། །།ཞེས་པ་འདི་ནི་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་གཞོན་ནུ་དཔལ་བའི་ཞལ་སྔ་ནས་གསར་འགྱུར་མཛད་པའི་འཕྲོ་ཅུང་ཟད་ལུས་པ། རྗེ་དམ་པ་དེའི་དགོངས་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པའི་སླད་དུ་འགྱུར་བར་གྱིས་ཤིག་ཅེས། ཞྭ་དམར་ཅོད་པན་འཛིན་པ་བཞི་པ། དཔལ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་གྲགས་པ་ཡེ་ཤེས་དཔལ་བཟང་པོའི་ཞལ་སྔ་ནས་བཀའ་སྩལ་བ་སྤྱི་བོས་མནོས་ཏེ། ཞ་ལུ་ལོ་ཙཱ་བ་འགོས་ཆོས་སྐྱོང་བཟང་པོས། ལུགས་གཉིས་ཀྱི་མདུན་ས་ཆེན་པོ་ཕོ་བྲང་སྣེའུ་གདོང་རྩེར། ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྗེ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ཆེན་པོ་དཔལ་ངག་གི་དབང་ཕྱུག་གྲགས་པ་ཕྱོགས་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་རྣམ་པར་རྒྱལ་བའི་དཔལ་གྱི་མངའ་ཐང་ཆེན་པོ་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་ལེགས་པར་བསྒྱུར་བའོ། །དུས་གསུམ་རྒྱལ་བ་སྐྱེད་མ་རྡོ་རྗེའི་མཚན་ཅན་ཟབ་མོའི་དགོངས་འགྲེལ་རབ་གསལ་བ། །ཀུན་མཁྱེན་གཉིས་པ་དབྱིག་གཉེན་ཞེས་གྲགས་དཔལ་ལྡན་ཤིང་རྟ་ཆེན་པོས་རྣམ་པར་བཀོད། །གང་དེ་ཁ་བ་ཅན་པའི་དཔལ་དུ་གཞོན་ནུའི་མཚན་ཅན་མཁས་གྲུབ་མཆོག་གིས་བསྒྱུར། །དེ་ཉིད་རྫོགས་པར་བསྒྱུར་བའི་དགེ་བས་འདྲེན་པ་མཆོག་དེའི་དགོངས་པ་རྫོགས་གྱུར་ཅིག །སླར་ཡང་རྒྱ་དཔེ་ལ་གཏུགས་ཤིང་སློབ་དཔོན་ཀ་མ་ལ་ཤཱི་ལས་མཛད་པའི་འགྲེལ་པར་བརྗོད་བྱ་རིས་མཐུན་པ་རྣམས་དང་སྦྱར་ཏེ་ཚིག་ཕྲད་དང་འཁྲུགས་སྡེབ་པ་སོགས་ཅུང་ཟད་ལེགས་ཆར་འགྱུར་བ་རྣམས་འབད་ཅིང་དག་པར་བགྱིས་སོ།། །།
translation: Etādāśīm arthagatiṃ niśāmya, yeṣāṃ mahāyānam abaddhau meba, tān asmano bedmi na bāsmano pi, guṇair abhābyān lasunāna baimi, hīno hi gāmbhīryam udāratāmbā, boddhunna śaknāti na cādhi moktuṃ, prāyeṇa coṃbaṃbidha eṣa lokaḥ, tenātra dharme khilatām prayātaḥ. The Extensive Commentary on the Seven Topics of the Noble Bhagavatī Prajñāpāramitā Vajracchedikā composed by Master Vasubandhu is finished. Thus, regarding this which had a little remainder left from the new translation made in the presence of the omniscient Zhönnu Pal, having received on my crown the command bestowed from the presence of the fourth Zhāmar crown-holder, the glorious Chökyi Drakpa Yeshe Pal Zangpo, saying, 'Please translate it so that the intention of that holy lord may be completely fulfilled!', the Zhalu translator Gö Chökyong Zangpo excellently translated it at the peak of the Neudong palace, the great meeting place of the two traditions, relying on the great glorious domain completely victorious in all directions of the great Dharma lord, the great Dharma king, the glorious Ngagi Wangchuk Drakpa. The very clear commentary on the profound intention of the mother who generates the conquerors of the three times, bearing the mark of the Vajra, was completely arrayed by the glorious great chariot renowned as the second omniscient one, Vasubandhu. That was translated as the glory of the snowy land by the supreme learned adept bearing the name Zhönnu. By the virtue of translating it completely, may the intention of that supreme guide be fulfilled! Once again, having consulted the Indian manuscript and compared it with those having similar subject matter in the commentary composed by Master Kamalaśīla, I made efforts and made accurate whatever could be somewhat improved, such as connective particles and disordered arrangements.

འདིར་འཛིན་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཡང་འཕགས་པ་རབ་འབྱོར་གྱིས་དོན་དམ་པར་རྣམ་པར་འཇོག་པར་བྱེད་དེ། བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་དོན་དེ་ཉིད་སྒྲུབ་པར་མཛད་པ། རིལ་པོར་འཛིན་པ་ཉིད་ནི་ཐ་སྙད་དེ་ཞེས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་ཏེ། ཅིས་ཤེས་པར་བྱེད་ན་ཐ་སྙད་ལས་སོ། །
